text_blocks.snippet: Walgreens sells both rapid antigen and PCR tests for COVID-19, but their accuracy varies. Rapid antigen tests, commonly available over-the-counter, are less sensitive than PCR tests and can produce false negatives, especially in individuals without symptoms. However, a positive result on a rapid antigen test is generally considered accurate. PCR tests, typically performed in labs or doctor's offices, are more sensitive and less prone to false negatives.

list.title: Rapid Antigen Tests:
list.snippet: These tests are convenient and provide quick results, but they are less sensitive than PCR tests. This means they may not detect the virus in the early stages of infection or in individuals with low viral loads.

list.title: PCR Tests:
list.snippet: PCR tests are more sensitive and accurate, making them less likely to produce a false negative result. However, they require processing in a lab, which can take longer to produce results.

list.title: False Positives:
list.snippet: False positives are unlikely with rapid antigen tests, according to Walgreens.

list.title: False Negatives:
list.snippet: False negatives are more common with rapid antigen tests, especially in asymptomatic individuals or those with low viral loads.

list.title: When to Repeat Testing:
list.snippet: Regardless of the test type, if a negative result is obtained, especially with a rapid antigen test, it is recommended to repeat testing following the instructions provided with the test kit, according to the FDA.
